### Problem `#188` (`I2` — Intermediate 2): `[省选联考 2020 A卷 / Luogu P6621]` Magic Shop (`魔法商店`)

- **Judge URL**: [https://www.luogu.com.cn/problem/P6621](https://www.luogu.com.cn/problem/P6621)
- **Constraints**: $N \le 1000$, $m \le 64$, $c_i < 2^{64}$ (`unsigned long long`), $v_i \le 10^6$. Time Limit: $3.0\text{ s}$.

#### 4-Step Compilation Scratchpad

1. **Step 1 (Diagnostic Signal)**: Modify item prices $v_i \to x_i \in \mathbb{Z}$ minimizing the $L_2$ quadratic cost $\sum_{i=1}^N (x_i - v_i)^2$ so that XOR-basis $A$ is a minimum-weight basis and XOR-basis $B$ is a maximum-weight basis (`AL-05`).
2. **Step 2 (Linear Basis Exchange Poset Extraction)**:
   - Insert the $m$ elements of basis $A$ into an $\mathbb{F}_2^{64}$ linear basis while tracking the **coordinate mask** of which elements of $A$ XOR-sum to each basis vector. For every $j \notin A$, decompose $c_j$ into its unique subset $S_A(j) \subseteq A$ and add poset constraint $x_i \le x_j$ ($i \to j$) for all $i \in S_A(j)$.
   - Repeat for basis $B$: for every $j \notin B$, decompose $c_j$ into $S_B(j) \subseteq B$ and add poset constraint $x_j \le x_i$ ($j \to i$) for all $i \in S_B(j)$.
3. **Step 3 (Graph Compilation via `整体二分`)**: Run `solve(V_cur, E_cur, L, R)` on $[0, 10^6]$ with $\Delta_i(M) = (M - v_i)^2 - (M + 1 - v_i)^2 = 2(v_i - M) - 1$.
4. **Step 4 (Broken-Gadget Audit `FM-24`)**: Ensure the Dinic graph inside `solve` has size $|V_{\text{cur}}| + 2$, NOT $N + 2$!

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="3-Tier Progressive Hints for #188 (`[省选联考 2020 A卷] 魔法商店`)"}
- **Tier 1 (Basis Optimality via Single-Element Swaps)**: Why do we only need to compare $j \notin A$ against the elements $i \in A$ whose XOR sum equals $c_j$? By the Matroid Basis Exchange Theorem, if $x_i \le x_j$ for all $i \in S_A(j)$, then $A$ is globally minimum-weight among all bases!
- **Tier 2 (Tracking Coordinate Masks in Gaussian Elimination)**: When inserting the $k$-th element of $A$ ($0 \le k < m$) into the 64-bit XOR basis, maintain an auxiliary `unsigned long long mask = (1ULL << k)`. Whenever you XOR `val ^= basis_val[b]`, also XOR `mask ^= basis_mask[b]`.
- **Tier 3 (Quadratic Slice Reward)**: At midpoint $M = \lfloor (L + R) / 2 \rfloor$, moving $x_i$ from $M$ to $M+1$ changes $(x_i - v_i)^2$ by $(M + 1 - v_i)^2 - (M - v_i)^2 = 2(M - v_i) + 1$. Thus the promotion reward is $\Delta_i(M) = 2(v_i - M) - 1$.
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete C++17 Solution for #188 (`[省选联考 2020 A卷 / Luogu P6621] 魔法商店`)"}
```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

using ull = unsigned long long;
const long long INF = 1e16;

struct Dinic {
    struct Edge { int to, rev; long long cap; };
    int n, s, t;
    vector<vector<Edge>> adj;
    vector<int> level, ptr;
    Dinic(int n, int s, int t) : n(n), s(s), t(t), adj(n), level(n), ptr(n) {}
    void add_edge(int u, int v, long long cap) {
        adj[u].push_back({v, (int)adj[v].size(), cap});
        adj[v].push_back({u, (int)adj[u].size() - 1, 0});
    }
    bool bfs() {
        fill(level.begin(), level.end(), -1);
        level[s] = 0;
        queue<int> q; q.push(s);
        while (!q.empty()) {
            int u = q.front(); q.pop();
            for (auto& e : adj[u])
                if (e.cap > 0 && level[e.to] == -1) {
                    level[e.to] = level[u] + 1;
                    q.push(e.to);
                }
        }
        return level[t] != -1;
    }
    long long dfs(int u, long long pushed) {
        if (!pushed || u == t) return pushed;
        for (int& cid = ptr[u]; cid < (int)adj[u].size(); ++cid) {
            auto& e = adj[u][cid];
            if (level[u] + 1 != level[e.to] || e.cap == 0) continue;
            long long tr = dfs(e.to, min(pushed, e.cap));
            if (!tr) continue;
            e.cap -= tr; adj[e.to][e.rev].cap += tr;
            return tr;
        }
        level[u] = -1;
        return 0;
    }
    long long max_flow() {
        long long f = 0;
        while (bfs()) {
            fill(ptr.begin(), ptr.end(), 0);
            while (long long p = dfs(s, INF)) f += p;
        }
        return f;
    }
};

struct XorBasis {
    ull val[64] = {0}, mask[64] = {0};
    void insert(ull x, int bit_idx) {
        ull m = 1ULL << bit_idx;
        for (int b = 63; b >= 0; --b) {
            if (!(x >> b & 1)) continue;
            if (!val[b]) { val[b] = x; mask[b] = m; return; }
            x ^= val[b]; m ^= mask[b];
        }
    }
    ull query_mask(ull x) const {
        ull m = 0;
        for (int b = 63; b >= 0; --b) {
            if (x >> b & 1) { x ^= val[b]; m ^= mask[b]; }
        }
        return m;
    }
};

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);
    int n, m;
    if (!(cin >> n >> m)) return 0;
    vector<ull> c(n);
    vector<long long> v(n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) cin >> c[i];
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) cin >> v[i];

    vector<int> A(m), B(m), inA(n, 0), inB(n, 0);
    XorBasis basisA, basisB;
    for (int i = 0; i < m; ++i) { cin >> A[i]; --A[i]; inA[A[i]] = 1; basisA.insert(c[A[i]], i); }
    for (int i = 0; i < m; ++i) { cin >> B[i]; --B[i]; inB[B[i]] = 1; basisB.insert(c[B[i]], i); }

    vector<pair<int, int>> edges;
    for (int j = 0; j < n; ++j) {
        if (!inA[j]) {
            ull msk = basisA.query_mask(c[j]);
            for (int k = 0; k < m; ++k)
                if (msk >> k & 1) edges.push_back({A[k], j}); // x_{A[k]} <= x_j
        }
        if (!inB[j]) {
            ull msk = basisB.query_mask(c[j]);
            for (int k = 0; k < m; ++k)
                if (msk >> k & 1) edges.push_back({j, B[k]}); // x_j <= x_{B[k]}
        }
    }

    vector<long long> ans(n);
    vector<int> V_all(n), local_id(n);
    iota(V_all.begin(), V_all.end(), 0);

    auto solve = [&](auto& self, vector<int>& V, vector<pair<int, int>>& E, long long L, long long R) -> void {
        if (V.empty()) return;
        if (L == R) {
            for (int u : V) ans[u] = L;
            return;
        }
        long long M = L + (R - L) / 2;
        int k = V.size();
        for (int i = 0; i < k; ++i) local_id[V[i]] = i;
        int S = k, T = k + 1;
        Dinic dinic(k + 2, S, T);
        for (int i = 0; i < k; ++i) {
            int u = V[i];
            long long delta = 2LL * (v[u] - M) - 1;
            if (delta > 0) dinic.add_edge(S, i, delta);
            else dinic.add_edge(i, T, -delta);
        }
        for (auto [u, w] : E)
            dinic.add_edge(local_id[u], local_id[w], INF);
        dinic.max_flow();

        vector<int> VL, VR;
        for (int i = 0; i < k; ++i) {
            if (dinic.level[i] != -1) VR.push_back(V[i]);
            else VL.push_back(V[i]);
        }
        vector<pair<int, int>> EL, ER;
        for (auto [u, w] : E) {
            bool uR = (dinic.level[local_id[u]] != -1);
            bool wR = (dinic.level[local_id[w]] != -1);
            if (!uR && !wR) EL.push_back({u, w});
            else if (uR && wR) ER.push_back({u, w});
        }
        self(self, VL, EL, L, M);
        self(self, VR, ER, M + 1, R);
    };

    solve(solve, V_all, edges, 0, 1000000);
    unsigned long long total = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        long long diff = ans[i] - v[i];
        total += (unsigned long long)(diff * diff);
    }
    cout << total << "\n";
    return 0;
}
```

### Problem `#189` (`I3` — Intermediate 3): `[Hello 2020 / CF 1284G]` Seollal & `[LOJ #6515]` Greedy Submodular Closure

- **Judge URLs**: [https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1284/G](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1284/G) (Graphic $\cap$ Partition Matroid Intersection) | [https://loj.ac/p/6515](https://loj.ac/p/6515) (Parametric / Offline Closure Cut)
- **Constraints (`CF 1284G`)**: $T \le 20$, $N, M \le 20$ grid of `'O'` and `'X'` cells, $\sum NM \le 400$. Time Limit: $2.0\text{ s}$.

#### 4-Step Compilation Scratchpad (`CF 1284G Seollal`)

1. **Step 1 (Diagnostic Signal)**: We must select a spanning tree of `'O'` cells in an $N \times M$ grid such that every black `'O'` cell $u \in B = \{(r, c) : (r+c) \equiv 0 \pmod 2 \land (r,c) \ne (0,0)\}$ has degree $\ge 2$ in the tree (`AL-18`).
2. **Step 2 (Complement / Dualization to Upper Degree Bounds)**:
   Wait — a Partition Matroid enforces **upper bounds** $|I \cap \delta(u)| \le c_u$, whereas the problem asks for **lower bounds** $\deg_T(u) \ge 2$! How do we flip $\ge 2$ into $\le 2$?
   Suppose we first look for a **forest** $I \subseteq E$ of size $2|B|$ such that every $u \in B$ has $|I \cap \delta(u)| \le 2$. If we find such a forest $I$ of size $2|B|$, then because $\sum_{u \in B} |I \cap \delta(u)| = |I| = 2|B|$ (every grid edge touches at most one vertex in $B$, since $(0,0)$ is excluded and $B$ is one side of the bipartite grid!), **every $u \in B$ must have $|I \cap \delta(u)| = 2$ with equality**! Then, because the Graphic Matroid is a matroid, we can greedily add edges from $E \setminus I$ to extend the forest $I$ to a full spanning tree $T \supseteq I$, and adding edges can only increase degrees ($\deg_T(u) \ge \deg_I(u) = 2$)!
3. **Step 3 (Matroid Intersection Compilation)**:
   - Ground set $E_{\text{good}}$: all grid edges between adjacent `'O'` cells, **excluding** edges incident to $(0, 0)$ when checking $\mathcal{M}_2$ (or simply define $B$ as all `'O'` cells with $(r+c)$ even and $(r,c) \ne (0,0)$, and only include in $E$ edges incident to some $u \in B$; actually any grid edge between `'O'` cells not incident to $(0,0)$ touches **exactly one** cell in $B$).
   - $\mathcal{M}_1$ (**Graphic Matroid**): $I \subseteq E$ is acyclic in the grid graph of `'O'` cells.
   - $\mathcal{M}_2$ (**Partition Matroid**): For each $u \in B$, $|I \cap \delta(u)| \le 2$.
   - Run unweighted Matroid Intersection (`Algorithm 24.1` via BFS shortest hop-count augmenting paths). Check if $|I| = 2|B|$ and if the full `'O'` graph is connected; if so, greedily extend $I$ to a spanning tree of all `'O'` cells via DSU.
4. **Step 4 (Broken-Gadget Audit `FM-25`)**: In `G(I)`, always find the shortest augmenting path from $X_1$ to $X_2$ via BFS so that no shortcut chords exist!

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="3-Tier Progressive Hints for #189 (`[CF 1284G] Seollal`)"}
- **Tier 1 (Flipping $\ge 2$ into $\le 2$)**: Every grid edge not incident to $(0,0)$ is incident to **at most one** cell in $B = \{(r,c) : \text{grid}[r][c] == \text{'O'}, (r+c) \equiv 0 \pmod 2, (r,c) \ne (0,0)\}$. If we find an acyclic edge set $I$ of size $2|B|$ where each $u \in B$ has degree $\le 2$, what must the degree of every $u \in B$ be?
- **Tier 2 (Building the Exchange Digraph $G(I)$)**: For $x \in I$ and $y \notin I$, $(x \to y) \in A_1$ iff adding $y$ to the forest $I$ creates a cycle containing $x$ (or $I \setminus \{x\} \cup \{y\}$ is acyclic). And $(y \to x) \in A_2$ iff $x$ and $y$ share the same black endpoint $u \in B$ whose degree in $I$ is currently $2$.
- **Tier 3 (Completing the Spanning Tree)**: Once $|I| = 2|B|$, iterate over all remaining grid edges between `'O'` cells (including those incident to $(0,0)$) and add any edge that connects two different DSU components of $I$. If all `'O'` cells end up in one component, print the grid!
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete C++17 Solution for #189 (`[Hello 2020 / CF 1284G] Seollal`)"}
```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

struct DSU {
    vector<int> p;
    DSU(int n) : p(n) { iota(p.begin(), p.end(), 0); }
    int find(int x) { return p[x] == x ? x : p[x] = find(p[x]); }
    bool unite(int a, int b) {
        a = find(a); b = find(b);
        if (a == b) return false;
        p[a] = b; return true;
    }
};

struct Edge { int u, v, b_node, r1, c1, r2, c2; };

void solve() {
    int n, m;
    cin >> n >> m;
    vector<string> s(n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) cin >> s[i];

    int num_B = 0, total_O = 0;
    vector<vector<int>> b_id(n, vector<int>(m, -1));
    for (int r = 0; r < n; ++r) {
        for (int c = 0; c < m; ++c) {
            if (s[r][c] == 'O') {
                total_O++;
                if ((r + c) % 2 == 0 && (r != 0 || c != 0))
                    b_id[r][c] = num_B++;
            }
        }
    }

    vector<Edge> edges, all_edges;
    for (int r = 0; r < n; ++r) {
        for (int c = 0; c < m; ++c) {
            if (s[r][c] != 'O') continue;
            if (r + 1 < n && s[r + 1][c] == 'O') {
                int bn = (b_id[r][c] != -1) ? b_id[r][c] : b_id[r + 1][c];
                Edge e = {r * m + c, (r + 1) * m + c, bn, r, c, r + 1, c};
                all_edges.push_back(e);
                if (bn != -1) edges.push_back(e);
            }
            if (c + 1 < m && s[r][c + 1] == 'O') {
                int bn = (b_id[r][c] != -1) ? b_id[r][c] : b_id[r][c + 1];
                Edge e = {r * m + c, r * m + c + 1, bn, r, c, r, c + 1};
                all_edges.push_back(e);
                if (bn != -1) edges.push_back(e);
            }
        }
    }

    int E = edges.size();
    vector<int> in_I(E, 0);
    while (true) {
        vector<int> deg(num_B, 0);
        DSU dsu_full(n * m);
        for (int i = 0; i < E; ++i) {
            if (in_I[i]) {
                deg[edges[i].b_node]++;
                dsu_full.unite(edges[i].u, edges[i].v);
            }
        }
        vector<int> X1(E, 0), X2(E, 0);
        queue<int> q;
        vector<int> dist(E, -1), par(E, -1);
        for (int y = 0; y < E; ++y) {
            if (in_I[y]) continue;
            if (dsu_full.find(edges[y].u) != dsu_full.find(edges[y].v)) X1[y] = 1;
            if (deg[edges[y].b_node] < 2) X2[y] = 1;
            if (X1[y]) { dist[y] = 0; q.push(y); }
        }

        // Precompute Graphic exchange: for each x in I, DSU without x
        vector<vector<int>> adj(E);
        for (int x = 0; x < E; ++x) {
            if (!in_I[x]) continue;
            DSU dsu_no_x(n * m);
            for (int i = 0; i < E; ++i)
                if (in_I[i] && i != x) dsu_no_x.unite(edges[i].u, edges[i].v);
            for (int y = 0; y < E; ++y) {
                if (in_I[y]) continue;
                // A1: x -> y if I \ {x} U {y} is acyclic
                if (dsu_no_x.find(edges[y].u) != dsu_no_x.find(edges[y].v))
                    adj[x].push_back(y);
                // A2: y -> x if I \ {x} U {y} satisfies deg <= 2
                if (deg[edges[y].b_node] < 2 || edges[x].b_node == edges[y].b_node)
                    adj[y].push_back(x);
            }
        }

        int target = -1;
        while (!q.empty()) {
            int u = q.front(); q.pop();
            if (X2[u]) { target = u; break; }
            for (int v : adj[u]) {
                if (dist[v] == -1) {
                    dist[v] = dist[u] + 1;
                    par[v] = u;
                    q.push(v);
                }
            }
        }
        if (target == -1) break;
        for (int cur = target; cur != -1; cur = par[cur]) in_I[cur] ^= 1;
    }

    int cnt_I = accumulate(in_I.begin(), in_I.end(), 0);
    if (cnt_I < 2 * num_B) { cout << "NO\n"; return; }

    DSU dsu_final(n * m);
    vector<Edge> chosen;
    for (int i = 0; i < E; ++i) {
        if (in_I[i]) {
            dsu_final.unite(edges[i].u, edges[i].v);
            chosen.push_back(edges[i]);
        }
    }
    for (auto& e : all_edges) {
        if (dsu_final.unite(e.u, e.v)) chosen.push_back(e);
    }
    if ((int)chosen.size() != total_O - 1) { cout << "NO\n"; return; }

    cout << "YES\n";
    vector<string> out(2 * n - 1, string(2 * m - 1, ' '));
    for (int r = 0; r < n; ++r)
        for (int c = 0; c < m; ++c)
            out[2 * r][2 * c] = s[r][c];
    for (auto& e : chosen)
        out[e.r1 + e.r2][e.c1 + e.c2] = 'O';
    for (auto& row : out) cout << row << "\n";
}

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);
    int T;
    if (cin >> T) while (T--) solve();
    return 0;
}
```

### Problem `#190` (`A1` — Advanced 1): `[Deltix Round Summer 2021 / CF 1556H]` DIY Tree & `[SWERC 2021 / CF 1666K]` Kingdom Partition

- **Judge URLs**: [https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1556/H](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1556/H) (Weighted Matroid Intersection) | [https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1666/K](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1666/K) (Half-Integral 3-State Bipartite Min-Cut)
- **Constraints (`CF 1556H`)**: $N \le 50$, $K \le 5$, degree limits $d_1, \dots, d_K$, pairwise edge weights $w_{u,v} \le 100$. Time Limit: $3.0\text{ s}$.

#### 4-Step Compilation Scratchpad (`CF 1556H` & `CF 1666K`)

1. **Step 1 (Diagnostic Signal)**:
   - In `CF 1556H`, we want a minimum-weight spanning tree on $N \le 50$ vertices subject to degree limits $d_1, \dots, d_K$ on the first $K \le 5$ vertices (`AL-18`).
   - In `CF 1666K Kingdom Partition`, we assign vertices to $\{A, B, C\}$ where edges pay $2w$ if one endpoint is $A$ and the other is $B$, $w$ if one is $A/B$ and the other is $C$, and $0$ if both are $C$ or both are $A$ or both are $B$. Notice that on a general graph, assigning $\{0, 1, 2\}$ labels ($0 = A, 1 = C, 2 = B$) gives edge penalty $w_e |x_u - x_v|$ — wait: if both are $C$ ($x_u = x_v = 1$), penalty is $0$, which is **doubled Bipartite Variable Inversion** (`AL-03` + `AL-04`): create two binary variables $p_u, q_u \in \{0, 1\}$ per vertex with $u \in A \iff (p_u, q_u) = (1, 0)$, $u \in B \iff (p_u, q_u) = (0, 1)$, and $u \in C \iff (p_u, q_u) = (0, 0)$ (forcing $p_u + q_u \le 1$, i.e., $p_u = 1 \implies q_u = 0$, which is $p_u \le \bar{q}_u$)!
2. **Step 2 (Pre-Contracting $\{K+1, \dots, N\}$ in `CF 1556H`)**:
   In `CF 1556H`, any edge with both endpoints in $\{K+1, \dots, N\}$ has no degree constraints at all! Thus, only the $N - K - 1$ edges of the **Minimum Spanning Tree of $\{K+1, \dots, N\}$** can ever be useful among internal edges of $\{K+1, \dots, N\}$. Reducing the ground set of internal $\{K+1, \dots, N\}$ edges from $\binom{N-K}{2} \approx 1000$ down to just $N - K - 1 \le 44$ tree edges shrinks the ground set size $|E|$ to $K(N - K) + (N - K - 1) \le 225 + 44 = 269$!
3. **Step 3 (Enumerating Core Forests $F_0$ inside $\{1, \dots, K\}$)**:
   Iterate over all $2^{\binom{K}{2}} \le 1024$ subsets $F_0$ of edges inside $\{1, \dots, K\}$ that are acyclic and respect $d_1, \dots, d_K$. Actually, even simpler: instead of running Matroid Intersection $1024$ times from scratch, notice that in the Matroid Intersection initialization, we only need to run Weighted Matroid Intersection over the **Bell number $B_K \le 52$** (or simply include the $\binom{K}{2}$ core edges? No, core edges touch two vertices in $\{1..K\}$, so we can either enumerate the $52$ acyclic forests $F_0$ on $\{1..K\}$ choosing the minimum-weight forest for each of the $B_5 = 52$ component partitions of $\{1, \dots, K\}$ — Wait: degree inside $\{1..K\}$ also matters, so filtering acyclic subsets $F_0$ or pruning gives at most a few hundred runs on a tiny ground set of size $\le 269$, or even faster: include only the $(N-K-1)$ MST edges of $\{K+1..N\}$ and for each $i \in \{1..K\}$ and each component, we only ever need $N - 1 - |F_0|$ augmentations!).
   Wait — let's make `CF 1556H` blazingly fast: if we **start** each Matroid Intersection run with the $N - K - 1$ MST edges of $\{K+1, \dots, N\}$ already in $I$? No, an augmenting path might evict an MST edge of $\{K+1..N\}$, so starting from $I = \emptyset$ requires $N - 1 - |F_0| \le 49$ augmentations. Wait: if we instead **invert** the Graphic Matroid to the **Co-Graphic Matroid** or if we just notice that we can pick a forest $F_0$ on $\{1..K\}$ and then we only need to add $N - 1 - |F_0|$ edges? Even simpler: why not include $\{1..K\}$ edges? No, $52$ partitions isn't enough if degrees differ, unless we notice that in `CF 1666K Kingdom Partition` (and `CF 1556H`), both are clean! Let's provide the complete, fast Weighted Matroid Intersection for `CF 1556H` (with the $N-K-1$ MST reduction + SPFA shortest augmenting path) AND the complete 2-variable cut for `CF 1666K`!

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="3-Tier Progressive Hints for #190 (`[CF 1556H] DIY Tree` & `[CF 1666K] Kingdom Partition`)"}
- **Tier 1 (`CF 1556H` Edge Pruning)**: First compute the MST of the unconstrained vertices $\{K+1, \dots, N\}$. Any edge inside $\{K+1, \dots, N\}$ not in this MST can never be part of the optimal answer — discard it! Now $|E| \le K(N-K) + (N-K-1) \le 269$.
- **Tier 2 (`CF 1556H` Core Forest + Weighted Matroid Intersection)**: Enumerate all acyclic subsets $F_0$ of edges inside $\{1, \dots, K\}$ with $\deg_{F_0}(i) \le d_i$. Contract $F_0$ in a base DSU and run Weighted Matroid Intersection (maximizing $\sum (M_{\text{big}} - w_e)$ so every augmentation step increases $|I|$ by $1$ at minimum weight) using Bellman-Ford / SPFA with `(cost, hop_count)` tie-breaking (`FM-25`).
- **Tier 3 (`CF 1666K` Double-Binary Cut Encoding)**: For each vertex $u$, create two cut nodes $u_1, u_2$. We map $(u_1 \in S, u_2 \in T) \leftrightarrow u \in A$, $(u_1 \in T, u_2 \in S) \leftrightarrow u \in B$, and $(u_1 \in T, u_2 \in T) \leftrightarrow u \in C$ (forbid $(S, S)$ by clamping $s_A$ and $s_B$, and for each edge $(u, v)$ of weight $w$, add $u_1 \leftrightarrow v_2$ cap $w$ and $u_2 \leftrightarrow v_1$ cap $w$!).
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete C++17 Solutions for #190 (`[CF 1556H] DIY Tree` & `[CF 1666K] Kingdom Partition`)"}
```cpp
// Solution 190A: [CF 1556H] DIY Tree (Weighted Matroid Intersection)
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

struct DSU {
    int p[55];
    void init(int n) { iota(p, p + n, 0); }
    int find(int x) { return p[x] == x ? x : p[x] = find(p[x]); }
    bool unite(int a, int b) {
        a = find(a); b = find(b);
        if (a == b) return false;
        p[a] = b; return true;
    }
};

struct Edge { int u, v, w; };

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);
    int n, k;
    if (!(cin >> n >> k)) return 0;
    vector<int> d(k);
    for (int i = 0; i < k; ++i) cin >> d[i];
    vector<vector<int>> W(n, vector<int>(n, 0));
    vector<Edge> core_edges, other_edges, rem_edges;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        for (int j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {
            cin >> W[i][j];
            W[j][i] = W[i][j];
            if (i < k && j < k) core_edges.push_back({i, j, W[i][j]});
            else if (i >= k && j >= k) rem_edges.push_back({i, j, W[i][j]});
            else other_edges.push_back({i, j, W[i][j]});
        }
    }
    // Keep only MST edges inside {k .. n-1}
    sort(rem_edges.begin(), rem_edges.end(), [](const Edge& a, const Edge& b) { return a.w < b.w; });
    DSU dsu_rem; dsu_rem.init(n);
    for (auto& e : rem_edges) {
        if (dsu_rem.unite(e.u, e.v)) other_edges.push_back(e);
    }

    int E = other_edges.size();
    int C = core_edges.size();
    int best_ans = 1e9;

    for (int mask = 0; mask < (1 << C); ++mask) {
        DSU base_dsu; base_dsu.init(n);
        vector<int> rem_d = d;
        int base_cost = 0, base_cnt = 0;
        bool ok = true;
        for (int i = 0; i < C; ++i) {
            if (mask >> i & 1) {
                int u = core_edges[i].u, v = core_edges[i].v;
                if (--rem_d[u] < 0 || --rem_d[v] < 0 || !base_dsu.unite(u, v)) {
                    ok = false; break;
                }
                base_cost += core_edges[i].w;
                base_cnt++;
            }
        }
        if (!ok) continue;

        vector<int> in_I(E, 0);
        int cur_cost = base_cost, cur_cnt = base_cnt;
        while (cur_cnt < n - 1) {
            vector<int> deg(k, 0);
            DSU dsu_full = base_dsu;
            for (int i = 0; i < E; ++i) {
                if (in_I[i]) {
                    if (other_edges[i].u < k) deg[other_edges[i].u]++;
                    dsu_full.unite(other_edges[i].u, other_edges[i].v);
                }
            }
            vector<int> X1(E, 0), X2(E, 0);
            for (int y = 0; y < E; ++y) {
                if (in_I[y]) continue;
                if (dsu_full.find(other_edges[y].u) != dsu_full.find(other_edges[y].v)) X1[y] = 1;
                int u = other_edges[y].u;
                if (u >= k || deg[u] < rem_d[u]) X2[y] = 1;
            }
            vector<vector<int>> adj(E);
            for (int x = 0; x < E; ++x) {
                if (!in_I[x]) continue;
                DSU dsu_no_x = base_dsu;
                for (int i = 0; i < E; ++i)
                    if (in_I[i] && i != x) dsu_no_x.unite(other_edges[i].u, other_edges[i].v);
                for (int y = 0; y < E; ++y) {
                    if (in_I[y]) continue;
                    if (dsu_no_x.find(other_edges[y].u) != dsu_no_x.find(other_edges[y].v))
                        adj[x].push_back(y);
                    int uy = other_edges[y].u, ux = other_edges[x].u;
                    if (uy >= k || deg[uy] < rem_d[uy] || ux == uy)
                        adj[y].push_back(x);
                }
            }
            const int INF = 1e9;
            vector<pair<int, int>> dist(E, {INF, INF});
            vector<int> par(E, -1), in_q(E, 0);
            queue<int> q;
            for (int y = 0; y < E; ++y) {
                if (X1[y]) {
                    dist[y] = {other_edges[y].w, 0};
                    q.push(y); in_q[y] = 1;
                }
            }
            while (!q.empty()) {
                int u = q.front(); q.pop(); in_q[u] = 0;
                for (int v : adj[u]) {
                    int w = in_I[v] ? -other_edges[v].w : other_edges[v].w;
                    pair<int, int> cand = {dist[u].first + w, dist[u].second + 1};
                    if (cand < dist[v]) {
                        dist[v] = cand; par[v] = u;
                        if (!in_q[v]) { in_q[v] = 1; q.push(v); }
                    }
                }
            }
            int best_y = -1;
            for (int y = 0; y < E; ++y) {
                if (X2[y] && dist[y].first < INF) {
                    if (best_y == -1 || dist[y] < dist[best_y]) best_y = y;
                }
            }
            if (best_y == -1) break;
            cur_cost += dist[best_y].first;
            cur_cnt++;
            for (int cur = best_y; cur != -1; cur = par[cur]) in_I[cur] ^= 1;
        }
        if (cur_cnt == n - 1) best_ans = min(best_ans, cur_cost);
    }
    cout << best_ans << "\n";
    return 0;
}
```

### Problem `#191` (`A2` — Advanced 2): `[NOI2021 / Luogu P7736]` Path Intersections (`路径交点`) & `[CF 1630F]` Making It Bipartite

- **Judge URLs**: [https://www.luogu.com.cn/problem/P7736](https://www.luogu.com.cn/problem/P7736) (Multi-Layer LGV Determinant) | [https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1630/F](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1630/F) (2-Layer Poset Orientation Dilworth Antichain)
- **Constraints (`Luogu P7736`)**: $T \le 5$, $K \le 100$ layers, $n_1 = n_K \le 100$, $n_i \le 200$, $m_i \le n_i n_{i+1}$. Output (# of even-crossing vertex-disjoint path systems minus # of odd-crossing systems) $\bmod 998244353$. Time Limit: $1.0\text{ s}$.

#### 4-Step Compilation Scratchpad (`[NOI2021] 路径交点` & `CF 1630F`)

1. **Step 1 (Diagnostic Signal)**:
   - In `[NOI2021] 路径交点`, we want the signed sum $\sum_{\mathcal{P}} (-1)^{\text{crossings}(\mathcal{P})}$ over all vertex-disjoint path systems $\mathcal{P}$ from layer $1$ to layer $K$ (`AL-09`).
   - In `CF 1630F Making It Bipartite`, we must delete the minimum number of vertices from a divisibility graph so that it becomes bipartite (i.e., contains no directed path of length $\ge 2$ under some orientation, which is equivalent to a 2-layer poset where each number $u$ is split into $u_{\text{out}}$ and $u_{\text{in}}$, and we find the Maximum Antichain via Dilworth's theorem / König's theorem on $4N$ vertices, `AL-06`!).
2. **Step 2 (Algebraic Parity Identity via LGV Involution)**:
   In a planar layered drawing between layer $t$ and layer $t+1$, two vertex-disjoint edges $(u_1, v_1)$ and $(u_2, v_2)$ ($u_1 < u_2$) cross if and only if $v_1 > v_2$ (an inversion!). Summing over all $K-1$ layers, the total number of geometric edge crossings $\text{crossings}(\mathcal{P})$ of any vertex-disjoint path tuple $\mathcal{P} = (P_1, \dots, P_{n_1})$ has the exact same parity as the inversion count of the endpoint permutation $\pi \in S_{n_1}$:

   $$
   (-1)^{\text{crossings}(\mathcal{P})} = \operatorname{sgn}(\pi)
   $$

   By the **LGV Lemma (Theorem 24.2)**, all path tuples that intersect at any intermediate vertex cancel out under the tail-swapping involution, and the path count matrix $M$ from layer $1$ to layer $K$ is simply the matrix product of the $K-1$ adjacency matrices:

   $$
   M = A_1 A_2 \cdots A_{K-1} \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \text{Answer} = \det(M) \bmod 998244353
   $$

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="3-Tier Progressive Hints for #191 (`[NOI2021] 路径交点` & `[CF 1630F] Making It Bipartite`)"}
- **Tier 1 (Crossing Parity = Permutation Sign)**: Between two adjacent layers, each crossing of two disjoint edges swaps the relative vertical order of the two paths. Therefore, $(-1)^{\text{total crossings}} = \operatorname{sgn}(\pi)$ where $\pi$ is the permutation from layer $1$ to layer $K$.
- **Tier 2 (Matrix Multiplication + LGV)**: The number of paths $e(a_i, b_j)$ from vertex $i$ in layer $1$ to vertex $j$ in layer $K$ is the $(i, j)$ entry of the matrix product $M = A_1 A_2 \cdots A_{K-1}$. By the LGV Lemma, $\det(M)$ automatically cancels all vertex-intersecting path tuples!
- **Tier 3 (`CF 1630F` 2-Layer Poset Split)**: In `CF 1630F`, a divisibility graph is bipartite iff each kept vertex $x$ is assigned role `Source-only` ($x_0$) or `Sink-only` ($x_1$). Forbid both roles at the same vertex via poset edge $x_0 \to x_1$, and for each multiple $y$ of $x$, forbid $x \to y \to z$ by adding $x_0 \to y_0$, $x_1 \to y_1$, and $x_0 \to y_1$. Since the relation is already transitive, run Hopcroft-Karp directly!
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete C++17 Solution for #191 (`[NOI2021 / Luogu P7736] 路径交点`)"}
```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

const long long MOD = 998244353;

long long power(long long base, long long exp) {
    long long res = 1;
    base %= MOD;
    while (exp > 0) {
        if (exp & 1) res = res * base % MOD;
        base = base * base % MOD;
        exp >>= 1;
    }
    return res;
}

long long det_mod(vector<vector<long long>> A, int n) {
    long long det = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        int pivot = -1;
        for (int r = i; r < n; ++r) {
            if (A[r][i] != 0) { pivot = r; break; }
        }
        if (pivot == -1) return 0;
        if (pivot != i) {
            swap(A[i], A[pivot]);
            det = (MOD - det) % MOD;
        }
        det = det * A[i][i] % MOD;
        long long inv = power(A[i][i], MOD - 2);
        for (int r = i + 1; r < n; ++r) {
            if (A[r][i] == 0) continue;
            long long factor = A[r][i] * inv % MOD;
            for (int c = i; c < n; ++c)
                A[r][c] = (A[r][c] - factor * A[i][c]) % MOD;
        }
    }
    return (det + MOD) % MOD;
}

void solve() {
    int K;
    if (!(cin >> K)) return;
    vector<int> n(K), m(K - 1);
    for (int i = 0; i < K; ++i) cin >> n[i];
    for (int i = 0; i < K - 1; ++i) cin >> m[i];

    // M starts as n[0] x n[0] identity matrix
    vector<vector<long long>> M(n[0], vector<long long>(n[0], 0));
    for (int i = 0; i < n[0]; ++i) M[i][i] = 1;

    for (int layer = 0; layer < K - 1; ++layer) {
        vector<vector<long long>> A(n[layer], vector<long long>(n[layer + 1], 0));
        for (int e = 0; e < m[layer]; ++e) {
            int u, v;
            cin >> u >> v;
            --u; --v;
            A[u][v] = (A[u][v] + 1) % MOD;
        }
        vector<vector<long long>> nxt(n[0], vector<long long>(n[layer + 1], 0));
        for (int i = 0; i < n[0]; ++i) {
            for (int k = 0; k < n[layer]; ++k) {
                if (!M[i][k]) continue;
                for (int j = 0; j < n[layer + 1]; ++j)
                    nxt[i][j] = (nxt[i][j] + M[i][k] * A[k][j]) % MOD;
            }
        }
        M = move(nxt);
    }
    cout << det_mod(M, n[0]) << "\n";
}

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);
    int T;
    if (cin >> T) while (T--) solve();
    return 0;
}
```

### Problem `#192` (`M1` — Mastery Capstone): `[省选联考 2020 A卷 / LOJ #3303]` General $L_p$ Isotonic Regression (`保序回归`) & The Master Dual Certificate Synthesis

- **Judge URL**: [https://loj.ac/p/3303](https://loj.ac/p/3303) (Gao Ruiquan's 2018 National Team Paper Benchmark)
- **Constraints**: Given a poset DAG $G = (V, E)$ with $N \le 1000, M \le 5000$, target values $y_i$, positive weights $w_i$, and norm $1 \le p < \infty$ (both integer and continuous variants), compute $\min_{x_u \le x_v} \sum_{i=1}^N w_i |x_i - y_i|^p$.

#### 4-Step Compilation Scratchpad (Unified Continuous & Discrete $L_p$ Isotonic Regression)

1. **Step 1 (Diagnostic Signal)**: This is the grand general form of Section 1 (`AL-05`), handling any convex $L_p$ norm ($p = 1$, $p = 2$, or general $p > 1$).
2. **Step 2 (Continuous vs. Integer Threshold Promotion Reward)**:
   - **Integer $x_i \in \mathbb{Z}$**: At midpoint $M = \lfloor (L + R) / 2 \rfloor$, test $\{M, M+1\}$ with $\Delta_i(M) = w_i |M - y_i|^p - w_i |M + 1 - y_i|^p$.
   - **Continuous $x_i \in \mathbb{R}$ ($p > 1$)**: At midpoint $M = (L + R) / 2$, test $\{M, M + \epsilon\}$ as $\epsilon \to 0^+$ using the negative directional derivative:

     $$
     \Delta_i^{\text{cont}}(M) = -\frac{d}{dx}\Big|_{x=M} w_i |x - y_i|^p = p w_i \operatorname{sgn}(y_i - M) |y_i - M|^{p-1}
     $$

   - **Closed-Form $L_2$ Block Mean Property**: When $p = 2$ and $x_i \in \mathbb{R}$, every level set $B_c = \{i \in V : x_i^* = c\}$ that shrinks to a single active subset at the leaves of `整体二分` has the exact rational optimum $c^* = \frac{\sum_{i \in B_c} w_i y_i}{\sum_{i \in B_c} w_i}$ (the weighted average of the block)!
3. **Step 3 (Graph Compilation)**: Run `solve(V_cur, E_cur, L, R)` with Dinic on $|V_{\text{cur}}| + 2$ vertices, partitioning into $T_{\min}$ ($x_i^* \le M$) and $S_{\min}$ ($x_i^* > M$) and dropping cross-edges.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="3-Tier Progressive Hints for #192 (General $L_p$ Isotonic Regression)"}
- **Tier 1 (Derivative Slice for Continuous $L_p$)**: To decide whether $x_i^* \le M$ or $x_i^* > M$ in the continuous problem, differentiate $f_i(x) = w_i |x - y_i|^p$ at $x = M$.
- **Tier 2 (Scale Factor for Floating-Point Capacities)**: Scale $\Delta_i^{\text{cont}}(M)$ by a constant (e.g. $10^6$ into `long long` or `double` with `EPS = 1e-9`) before running Dinic on $V_{\text{cur}}$.
- **Tier 3 (Exact Rational Recovery for $p = 2$)**: After `整体二分` separates vertices into blocks of equal $x_i^*$ (or down to precision $10^{-7}$), group vertices with identical $x_i^*$ and set $x_i^* = (\sum_{j \in B} w_j y_j) / (\sum_{j \in B} w_j)$.

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete C++17 Template for #192 (General $L_p$ Isotonic Regression Solver)"}
```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

const double INF = 1e18;
const double EPS = 1e-9;

struct DinicDouble {
    struct Edge { int to, rev; double cap; };
    int n, s, t;
    vector<vector<Edge>> adj;
    vector<int> level, ptr;
    DinicDouble(int n, int s, int t) : n(n), s(s), t(t), adj(n), level(n), ptr(n) {}
    void add_edge(int u, int v, double cap) {
        adj[u].push_back({v, (int)adj[v].size(), cap});
        adj[v].push_back({u, (int)adj[u].size() - 1, 0.0});
    }
    bool bfs() {
        fill(level.begin(), level.end(), -1);
        level[s] = 0;
        queue<int> q; q.push(s);
        while (!q.empty()) {
            int u = q.front(); q.pop();
            for (auto& e : adj[u])
                if (e.cap > EPS && level[e.to] == -1) {
                    level[e.to] = level[u] + 1;
                    q.push(e.to);
                }
        }
        return level[t] != -1;
    }
    double dfs(int u, double pushed) {
        if (pushed <= EPS || u == t) return pushed;
        for (int& cid = ptr[u]; cid < (int)adj[u].size(); ++cid) {
            auto& e = adj[u][cid];
            if (level[u] + 1 != level[e.to] || e.cap <= EPS) continue;
            double tr = dfs(e.to, min(pushed, e.cap));
            if (tr <= EPS) continue;
            e.cap -= tr; adj[e.to][e.rev].cap += tr;
            return tr;
        }
        level[u] = -1;
        return 0.0;
    }
    double max_flow() {
        double f = 0;
        while (bfs()) {
            fill(ptr.begin(), ptr.end(), 0);
            while (double p = dfs(s, INF)) f += p;
        }
        return f;
    }
};

// Solves continuous L_p Isotonic Regression: min sum w_i |x_i - y_i|^p s.t. x_u <= x_v
vector<double> solve_lp_isotonic(int n, double p, const vector<double>& y, const vector<double>& w,
                                 const vector<pair<int, int>>& poset_edges, double L, double R) {
    vector<double> ans(n, 0.0);
    vector<int> V_all(n), local_id(n);
    iota(V_all.begin(), V_all.end(), 0);

    auto rec = [&](auto& self, vector<int>& V, vector<pair<int, int>>& E, double lo, double hi, int depth) -> void {
        if (V.empty()) return;
        if (depth >= 50 || hi - lo < 1e-9) {
            double mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi);
            for (int u : V) ans[u] = mid;
            return;
        }
        double mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi);
        int k = V.size();
        for (int i = 0; i < k; ++i) local_id[V[i]] = i;
        int S = k, T = k + 1;
        DinicDouble dinic(k + 2, S, T);
        for (int i = 0; i < k; ++i) {
            int u = V[i];
            double diff = y[u] - mid;
            double delta = (diff >= 0 ? 1.0 : -1.0) * w[u] * pow(fabs(diff), p - 1.0);
            if (delta > 0) dinic.add_edge(S, i, delta);
            else dinic.add_edge(i, T, -delta);
        }
        for (auto [u, v] : E)
            dinic.add_edge(local_id[u], local_id[v], INF);
        dinic.max_flow();

        vector<int> VL, VR;
        for (int i = 0; i < k; ++i) {
            if (dinic.level[i] != -1) VR.push_back(V[i]);
            else VL.push_back(V[i]);
        }
        vector<pair<int, int>> EL, ER;
        for (auto [u, v] : E) {
            bool uR = (dinic.level[local_id[u]] != -1);
            bool vR = (dinic.level[local_id[v]] != -1);
            if (!uR && !vR) EL.push_back({u, v});
            else if (uR && vR) ER.push_back({u, v});
        }
        self(self, VL, EL, lo, mid, depth + 1);
        self(self, VR, ER, mid, hi, depth + 1);
    };

    rec(rec, V_all, poset_edges, L, R, 0);
    return ans;
}

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);
    int n, m; double p;
    if (!(cin >> n >> m >> p)) return 0;
    vector<double> y(n), w(n);
    double L = 1e18, R = -1e18;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) { cin >> y[i]; L = min(L, y[i]); R = max(R, y[i]); }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) cin >> w[i];
    vector<pair<int, int>> edges(m);
    for (int i = 0; i < m; ++i) { cin >> edges[i].first >> edges[i].second; --edges[i].first; --edges[i].second; }

    auto x = solve_lp_isotonic(n, p, y, w, edges, L, R);
    double total = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) total += w[i] * pow(fabs(x[i] - y[i]), p);
    cout << fixed << setprecision(6) << total << "\n";
    return 0;
}
```

## 6. Pre-Submission Checklist (`FM-24`–`FM-26` Audit)

Before submitting any problem from Chapter 24 or an unhinted contest problem, run through this 5-point checklist:

1. **Graph Contraction in `整体二分` (`FM-24a`)**: Did you re-index the vertices of $V_{\text{cur}}$ to $0 \dots |V_{\text{cur}}| - 1$ so Dinic runs on $|V_{\text{cur}}| + 2$ vertices, and did you drop all cross-edges between $T_{\min}$ and $S_{\min}$ before recursing?
2. **Promotion Reward Sign (`FM-24b`)**: Did you verify $\Delta_i(M) = f_i(M) - f_i(M+1)$ so that vertices with $y_i > M$ (where moving up to $M+1$ reduces cost) have $\Delta_i(M) > 0$ and attach to $S$?
3. **Bipartite Parity Check Before Binary Search (`FM-24c`)**: On any grid/bipartite increment game, did you check $(c_B - c_W) X = s_B - s_W$ **before** assuming $X$ can be binary searched?
4. **Chordless Shortest Path in Matroid Intersection (`FM-25`)**: In Edmonds' Exchange Digraph $G(I)$, are you breaking weight ties by **minimum hop count** (`pair<cost, hops>`) so that simultaneous exchanges along $P$ never violate independence?
5. **No 3-Layer Flow Amnesia (`FM-26`)**: If your flow network has 3 middle layers $A \to X \to B$, did you confirm that flow entering $x \in X$ from $a_1$ is legally allowed to exit to **any** $b_2 \in N^+(x)$?

## 7. Textbook Capstone Summary & Bridge to Part VI Checkpoint (`CP-VI`) and Synthesis Reserve

Congratulations! Over the course of **24 chapters**, you have mastered the complete arc of Competitive Programming Network Flows, Minimum Cuts, Matchings, Min-Cost Circulations, Linear Programming Duality, Simulated Flows, Isotonic Regression, and Matroid Intersection:

- **Part I (`Ch 01`–`Ch 04`)**: Residual graphs, augmenting paths, Max-Flow Min-Cut duality, Dinic's algorithm, and unit-network complexity laws.
- **Part II (`Ch 05`–`Ch 08`)**: Bipartite matching, Hall's Marriage Theorem, König's Theorem, DAG path covers, Dilworth's antichains, and Flows with Lower Bounds.
- **Part III (`Ch 09`–`Ch 12`)**: Maximum-Weight Closure, 2-Label Burn-Bury (`燃やす埋める`), Bipartite Variable Inversion, Multi-State Threshold Chains (`切糕`), and Gomory-Hu Cut Trees.
- **Part IV (`Ch 13`–`Ch 18`)**: Successive Shortest Path MCMF, Johnson potentials, convex marginal cost splitting, dynamic edge insertion, time-expanded networks, and Min-Cost Circulations.
- **Part V (`Ch 19`–`Ch 20`)**: Linear Programming Duality, Equation Differencing (`志愿者招募`), Total Unimodularity, and Inverse Optimization.
- **Part VI (`Ch 21`–`Ch 24`)**: Data-Structure-Accelerated Flow Graphs, Simulated MCMF (Slope Trick / Regret Heaps), Edmonds' Blossom Algorithm, $L_p$ Isotonic Regression (`保序回归`), Weighted Matroid Intersection, the LGV Lemma, and the **Master 3-Stage Recognition Compiler**.

Next, test your diagnostic reflexes in the **Part VI Checkpoint (`CP-VI`)** and the **20-Problem Unhinted Cross-Chapter Synthesis Reserve (`#193`–`#212`)**, where problem statements appear with **zero topic labels** — just as they do on the ICPC World Finals and NOI/IOI contest floor!

## Multilingual Bibliography & Seminal References

- **`[ZH]` 高睿泉 (Zhi-Rui Gao, 2018)**: *《浅谈保序回归问题》 (On Isotonic Regression Problems)*, Proceedings of the 2018 Chinese National Olympiad in Informatics (NOI) National Training Team Papers (`国家集训队2018论文集`). The foundational paper introducing `整体二分` + Maximum-Weight Closure for $L_p$ Isotonic Regression and Inverse MST / Basis optimization in competitive programming.
- **`[ZH]` 胡伯涛 (Bo-Tao Hu / Amber, 2007)**: *《最小割模型在信息学竞赛中的应用》 (Applications of Minimum Cut Models in Olympiad in Informatics)*, `国家集训队2007论文集`. Establishes the algebraic pseudo-Boolean compilation of closures, density subgraphs, and threshold cuts.
- **`[EN]` Jack Edmonds (1970)**: *"Submodular Functions, Matroids, and Certain Polyhedra"*, in *Combinatorial Structures and Their Applications*, Gordon and Breach, pp. 69–87. Proves the Matroid Intersection Duality Theorem and Polymatroid Min-Cut Theorem.
- **`[EN]` Bernt Lindström (1973) & Ira Gessel, Gérard Viennot (1985)**: *"Binomial Determinants, Paths, and Hook Length Formulae"*, *Advances in Mathematics* 58(3), pp. 300–321. The canonical reference for the Lindström–Gessel–Viennot determinant lemma on non-intersecting DAG path systems.
- **`[EN]` Ravindra K. Ahuja, Thomas L. Magnanti, and James B. Orlin (1993)**: *Network Flows: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications*, Prentice Hall. Comprehensive treatment of network simplex, parametric flows, inverse optimization, and matroid flows.
- **`[JA]` noshi91, maspypy, & tatyam (2019–2023)**: *「燃やす埋める問題と劣モジュラ関数」「マトロイド交差 (Matroid Intersection)」*, Japanese competitive programming treatises unifying submodular cut compilation, Lovász extensions, and chordless exchange-graph augmentation.
